posts.name: Reverend Pete
posts.cooked:
Mint.

 

Got scary at the end, but it was helpful sort of laying low, drawing cards and setting up heroes for the first several turns until Spite flipped.  I put 4 victims under the safehouse the turn before the flip. Unity was doing some damage: she had 6-7 bots (1 raptor) out for a couple of turns prior to the flip (kept alive by Stealth Bot), KNYFE had a bunch of boosting cards out (and the damage reduction one--that was very helpful), and right before Spite flipped, KNYFE played Overdo It, which was KEY for 2 mega-KNYFE turns of Energy Burns and Battle Field Experiences right after the flip.

 

After the flip, I think Spite had 50 HP, but after KNYFE had a turn, it was down to the mid-20s. Unity ended up incapping, as did Expatriette on that last round, but their incap powers were what let KNYFE play the extra cards and use extra powers to finish Spite off.

 

KNYFE had 7HP, Nightmist had 10HP and Unity and Expatriette were out.

posts.name: deddragon
posts.cooked:
I was reading the description (in my head) in a movie trailer narrator voice when I suddenly realized that actually WAS the theme

No Mint for me this time. I completely forgot how to battle Spite and kept using powers, which of course only served to beat myself up. I tried to rally, but too little too late. He did 29 damage to himself on the flip, but by then I couldn’t withstand the barrage.

The second time through I set up a lot more. Knyfe and Expat skipped every power phase, while Nightmist had no trouble weathering the damage and Unity had to put out Bots.
Only managed 19 damage on the flip this time (didn’t take out the Collateral Damage) but the Raptors and Volatile Parts made up for it.
Unity went down right after the flip. Knyfe and Expatriette got 1 turn each, both taking themselves out to deal some damage.
With Spite under 15 and Nightmist at full HP, it was an attrition game. Spite would return the Ring and Mist Form to her hand (keeping out the Amulet), Knyfe had her play the Ring, Unity kept her HP up, and Expat added projectile damage for the eventual break-out power use. All Nightmist did was kept playing Mistform and wait. Then Zhu Long thought Spite looked tasty and a single Lash ended it.

Not the prettiest Near Mint, but it’s there.

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
I don't know how that's possible either, with Spite's retaliatory damage.  He heals way too much when you use powers, and the one-shots of these guys just aren't enough to keep up with the rest of his healing.

I did get mint, same way as everyone else, with Nightmist tanking like mad thanks to everyone else's incaps.  Well, KNYFE's and Unity's incaps, anyway.  This play order works beautifully once the game gets to that point, since Nightmist will have a full stack of equipment and ongoings on her turn.  Finished with Nightmist at 19, with the final turn involving Spite getting stabbed by a Shinobi Assassin, then hit three times with Oblivion (one of them being a redirect), then stabbed by the Assassin a second time, and finally getting shot 4 times with Expatriette's incap power boosted by an Elder Ring.  Pretty sweet.

posts.name: just.a.smith
posts.cooked: It mainly involved liberal use of Raptor Bots and a T1 Stealth Bot.  Stealth Bot + Liquid Nitrogen Rounds means you get a round of no retaliatory damage, and in general I was just more willing to not use powers if they weren't helping me, especially once all three Mysterious Ceremonies were in play.  Combine with a couple of Mistbounds and by the end of the game, Spite only had three of his drugs in play.  Bee Bot was great for handling Master of the Temple getting The True Form.  It helps that I never saw a Lab Raid.  Expatriette didn't do a ton except for a few critical Nitrogen Rounds and playing enough Equipment to always be able to pick things up.  K.N.Y.F.E was... also there, I guess; she at least was able to get some good damage in.  Really this is Unity and Nightmist's show.

posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked:
Mint, Nightmist at 20, everyone else incapped. KNYFE and Unity both did some good work, Expat didn't get to do a whole lot except use a Hastily Augmented Shotgun for 6 and keep cycling stuff into play so the others could stay set up. I never saw a single ammo card. Would have been nice to have Liquid N2 Rounds but I ended up not needing them.

Wrecking Uppercut helped me get to the flip faster, and once he flipped, I cut loose with two Overdo It powered KNYFE turns and one big Unity turn. Volatile Parts helped knock him down a bit as well. I chose order poorly on the last Apprentice Poisoner I saw, but it only cost me 1 HP on him and it didn't matter - Nightmist was over 20 when everyone else went down, and Spite was already down to 14, so the environment was all over him and not me.

I think I'll give this another whirl for laughs later to see if I can do a little better.
